title: Kyiv's Mayor Says Russian Strikes Are Hitting the City's Key Services
summary:
Kyiv, the capital of Ukraine, is under heavy attack from Russia. The city's mayor, Vitaliy Klitschko, says the strikes are "tearing Kyiv apart." He calls the situation "very dramatic." He says Russia is hitting critical services such as logistics and housing.

One big target has been the Pivdennyi bridge. It is one of the main routes across the Dnipro River, which divides the western and eastern parts of the city. A Russian drone hit the bridge overnight. On Friday evening it was hit again, the fourth time in two days. Now no metro trains or cars can cross it. There are also restrictions on Kyiv's two other key bridges, so traffic jams have spread across the city. About three million people live in Kyiv, and many of them rely on the metro.

Data centers, which store information for the internet, have also been hit recently. That caused internet outages. Ukraine's state emergency service said one person was killed when a residential building was hit overnight.

The leaders describe the attacks in different ways. The mayor says Russia wants to "sow panic." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Russian President Vladimir Putin decided in early September that "there are no rules now." Putin says Russia is answering Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy sites and oil refineries.

After a crisis meeting of Kyiv's defence council, Klitschko said the city would get through this with the joint efforts of the people who care about it.
why_it_matters: Attacks on bridges, internet and housing affect how ordinary people travel, communicate and live every day.
